title: Returning Your Shopping Cart Won't Save You From a Tornado Cow
description:
The shopping cart test, settled by physics: a tornado does not care if you returned your cart.

The useless facts:
- An EF5 tornado, the top of the Enhanced Fujita scale, has estimated winds over 200 mph.
- Tornadoes really have picked up cattle; a single cow can weigh over 600 kg (about 1,300 lb).
- Returning your cart to the corral is still the right thing to do. Just not a force field.

Useless Facts is our series of true facts nobody needed. Do you always return your cart?

Sources:
- NOAA / National Weather Service, Enhanced Fujita scale and EF5 tornadoes (winds over 200 mph): https://www.weather.gov/arx/ef5tornadoes
- The Weather Network, Could a cow really get swept up by a tornado? (cows over 600 kg; farm animals picked up): https://www.theweathernetwork.com/en/news/science/explainers/could-a-cow-really-get-swept-up-by-a-tornado
- weather.com, EF5 tornadoes (winds estimated over 200 mph): https://weather.com/storms/tornado/news/2024-05-22-ef5-tornadoes-us-since-1950
